item.title: Gallipolis City Commission hears from concerned residents regarding road conditions
item.description: GALLIPOLIS, Ohio — The Gallipolis City Commission addressed the city’s proposed budget and heard pleas regarding deteriorating infrastructure during a regular meeting Tuesday evening at the Municipal Building.

item.title: Hope Gas announces $250M pipeline expansion in Mason County expected to create 600 jobs
item.description: POINT PLEASANT, W.Va. — Hope Gas on Tuesday announced a $250 million pipeline expansion in Mason County, a project expected to create more than 600 construction jobs and strengthen energy service for homes, businesses and manufacturers.

item.title: Low-dose radiation emerging as treatment option for osteoarthritis, Holzer physician says
item.description: GALLIPOLIS, Ohio — Osteoarthritis affects millions of people each year and remains one of the leading causes of disability in the United States, according to the World Health Organization.

item.title: ODNR seeking nominations for 2026 Ohio Natural Resources Hall of Fame
item.description: COLUMBUS, Ohio — The Ohio Department of Natural Resources is seeking nominations for the 2026 class of the Ohio Natural Resources Hall of Fame, one of the state’s highest honors recognizing lifetime achievements in protecting and preserving Ohio’s natural resources.

item.title: Meigs County jury convicts man on two rape charges
item.description: POMEROY, Ohio — A Meigs County jury has found a man guilty on two counts of rape following a two-day trial in the Meigs County Court of Common Pleas.

item.title: International study highlights literacy gains from Dolly Parton’s Imagination Library program
item.description: COLUMBUS, Ohio — Ohio Gov. Mike DeWine and First Lady Fran DeWine joined Dolly Parton’s Imagination Library of Ohio in highlighting the results of a new international study showing the program’s positive impact on children’s literacy and family reading habits.

item.description: CHARLESTON — Hunters harvested 92,553 white-tailed deer during West Virginia’s 2025-26 hunting seasons, a 17 percent decrease from the 111,646 deer taken in 2024 and 14 percent below the five-year average of 107,434, according to the West Virginia Division of…
